title: 7 C.F.R. § 29.1079 — Variegated (K).
creator: Agricultural Marketing Service (Standards, Inspections, Marketing Practices), Department Of Agriculture
description: Code of Federal Regulations, Title 7 (Agriculture), Part 29 (Tobacco Inspection). Text from the eCFR as of 2026-10-26 (unofficial editorial compilation; the official edition is the annual CFR). Any tobacco that does not blend with the normal colors of the types; any leaf of which 20 percent or more of its surface is grayish, mottled, bleached, doty-faced, scalded, or sunbaked. (See Rule 15.).

title: 7 C.F.R. § 29.1080 — Variegated dark red (KD).
creator: Agricultural Marketing Service (Standards, Inspections, Marketing Practices), Department Of Agriculture
description: Code of Federal Regulations, Title 7 (Agriculture), Part 29 (Tobacco Inspection). A dark brownish-red discoloration which usually results from excessive sunbaking during the growing process or from storing cured tobacco over extended periods of time. Any leaf of which 20 percent or more of its surface is dark brownish-red may be described as variegated dark.

title: 7 C.F.R. § 29.1081 — Variegated red or scorched (KR).
creator: Agricultural Marketing Service (Standards, Inspections, Marketing Practices), Department Of Agriculture
description: Code of Federal Regulations, Title 7 (Agriculture), Part 29 (Tobacco Inspection). Text from the eCFR as of 2026-10-26 (unofficial editorial compilation; the official edition is the annual CFR). A red discoloration which usually results from excessive heat in the curing process. Any leaf of which 20 percent or more of its surface has been reddened in the curing process may be described as variegated red or scorched. (See Rule 16.).

creator: Agricultural Marketing Service (Standards, Inspections, Marketing Practices), Department Of Agriculture
description: Code of Federal Regulations, Title 7 (Agriculture), Part 29 (Tobacco Inspection). The portion or portions of the web of tobacco leaves which have been lost or rendered less serviceable for use in tobacco products, including: (a) Portions which have decomposed or largely decomposed by field diseases and field-firing, pole-burning, bulk-burning; (b) portions which are dead.

description: Code of Federal Regulations, Title 7 (Agriculture), Part 29 (Tobacco Inspection). Wet applies to any tobacco which is not damaged but which is likely to damage if treated in the customary manner. (See Rule 22.).

title: 7 C.F.R. § 29.1084 — Whitish-lemon (LL).

description: Code of Federal Regulations, Title 7 (Agriculture), Part 29 (Tobacco Inspection). Text from the eCFR as of 2026-10-26 (unofficial editorial compilation; the official edition is the annual CFR). A whitish-yellow color which usually results during wet growing seasons when rain leaches or washes out the yellow color from the leaf. Any leaf of which 20 percent or more of its leaf surface has whitish-yellow color may be described as whitish-lemon.

title: 7 C.F.R. § 29.1085 — Width.
creator: Agricultural Marketing Service (Standards, Inspections, Marketing Practices), Department Of Agriculture
description: Code of Federal Regulations, Title 7 (Agriculture), Part 29 (Tobacco Inspection). Text from the eCFR as of 2026-10-26 (unofficial editorial compilation; the official edition is the annual CFR). The relative breadth of a tobacco leaf expressed in relation to its length. Width, as an element of quality, does not apply to tobacco in strip form. (See Elements of Quality Chart.).

description: Code of Federal Regulations, Title 7 (Agriculture), Part 29 (Tobacco Inspection). Tobacco attributes or characteristics which constitute quality are designated as elements of quality. The range within each element is expressed by the use of words or.

creator: Agricultural Marketing Service (Standards, Inspections, Marketing Practices), Department Of Agriculture
description: Code of Federal Regulations, Title 7 (Agriculture), Part 29 (Tobacco Inspection). Text from the eCFR as of 2026-10-26 (unofficial editorial compilation; the official edition is the annual CFR). title: 7 C.F.R. § 29.1107 — Rule 1.
creator: Agricultural Marketing Service (Standards, Inspections, Marketing Practices), Department Of Agriculture
description: Code of Federal Regulations, Title 7 (Agriculture), Part 29 (Tobacco Inspection). Text from the eCFR as of 2026-10-26 (unofficial editorial compilation; the official edition is the annual CFR). Each grade shall be treated as a subdivision of a particular type. When the grade is stated in an inspection certificate, the type also shall be stated.

title: 7 C.F.R. § 29.1108 — Rule 2.
creator: Agricultural Marketing Service (Standards, Inspections, Marketing Practices), Department Of Agriculture
description: Code of Federal Regulations, Title 7 (Agriculture), Part 29 (Tobacco Inspection). Text from the eCFR as of 2026-10-26 (unofficial editorial compilation; the official edition is the annual CFR). The determination of a grade shall be based upon a thorough examination of a lot of tobacco or of an official sample of the lot.

title: 7 C.F.R. § 29.1109 — Rule 3.
creator: Agricultural Marketing Service (Standards, Inspections, Marketing Practices), Department Of Agriculture
description: Code of Federal Regulations, Title 7 (Agriculture), Part 29 (Tobacco Inspection). Text from the eCFR as of 2026-10-26 (unofficial editorial compilation; the official edition is the annual CFR). In drawing an official sample from a hogshead or other package of tobacco, three or more breaks shall be made at such points and in such manner as the inspector or sampler may find necessary to determine the kinds of tobacco and the percentage.

title: 7 C.F.R. § 29.1110 — Rule 4.
creator: Agricultural Marketing Service (Standards, Inspections, Marketing Practices), Department Of Agriculture
description: Code of Federal Regulations, Title 7 (Agriculture), Part 29 (Tobacco Inspection). Text from the eCFR as of 2026-10-26 (unofficial editorial compilation; the official edition is the annual CFR). All standard grades must be clean unless otherwise noted by a special factor.

creator: Agricultural Marketing Service (Standards, Inspections, Marketing Practices), Department Of Agriculture
description: Code of Federal Regulations, Title 7 (Agriculture), Part 29 (Tobacco Inspection). Text from the eCFR as of 2026-10-26 (unofficial editorial compilation; the official edition is the annual CFR). The grade assigned to any lot of tobacco shall be a true representation of the tobacco at the time of inspection and certification. If, at any time, it is found that a lot of tobacco does not comply with the specifications of the grade.

title: 7 C.F.R. § 29.1112 — Rule 6.
creator: Agricultural Marketing Service (Standards, Inspections, Marketing Practices), Department Of Agriculture
description: Code of Federal Regulations, Title 7 (Agriculture), Part 29 (Tobacco Inspection). Text from the eCFR as of 2026-10-26 (unofficial editorial compilation; the official edition is the annual CFR). A lot of tobacco on the marginal line between two colors shall be placed in the color with which it best corresponds with respect to body or other associated elements of quality.

title: 7 C.F.R. § 29.1113 — Rule 7.
creator: Agricultural Marketing Service (Standards, Inspections, Marketing Practices), Department Of Agriculture
description: Code of Federal Regulations, Title 7 (Agriculture), Part 29 (Tobacco Inspection). Any lot of tobacco which meets the specifications of two grades shall be placed in the higher grade. Any lot of tobacco on the marginal line between two grades shall be placed in the lower grade.

creator: Agricultural Marketing Service (Standards, Inspections, Marketing Practices), Department Of Agriculture
description: Code of Federal Regulations, Title 7 (Agriculture), Part 29 (Tobacco Inspection). Text from the eCFR as of 2026-10-26 (unofficial editorial compilation; the official edition is the annual CFR). A lot of tobacco meets the specifications of a grade when it is not lower in any degree of any element of quality than the minimum specifications of such grade.

title: 7 C.F.R. § 29.1115 — Rule 9.
creator: Agricultural Marketing Service (Standards, Inspections, Marketing Practices), Department Of Agriculture
description: Code of Federal Regulations, Title 7 (Agriculture), Part 29 (Tobacco Inspection). Text from the eCFR as of 2026-10-26 (unofficial editorial compilation; the official edition is the annual CFR). title: 7 C.F.R. § 29.1116 — Rule 10.
creator: Agricultural Marketing Service (Standards, Inspections, Marketing Practices), Department Of Agriculture
description: Code of Federal Regulations, Title 7 (Agriculture), Part 29 (Tobacco Inspection). title: 7 C.F.R. § 29.1117 — Rule 11.
creator: Agricultural Marketing Service (Standards, Inspections, Marketing Practices), Department Of Agriculture
description: Code of Federal Regulations, Title 7 (Agriculture), Part 29 (Tobacco Inspection). Text from the eCFR as of 2026-10-26 (unofficial editorial compilation; the official edition is the annual CFR). Interpretations, the use of specifications, and the meaning of terms shall be in accordance with determinations or clarifications made by the Chief of the Marketing Programs Branch and approved by the Director.

title: 7 C.F.R. § 29.1118 — Rule 12.
creator: Agricultural Marketing Service (Standards, Inspections, Marketing Practices), Department Of Agriculture
description: Code of Federal Regulations, Title 7 (Agriculture), Part 29 (Tobacco Inspection). Minor irregularities which do not affect over one percent of the tobacco shall be overlooked.

title: 7 C.F.R. § 29.1119 — Rule 13.
creator: Agricultural Marketing Service (Standards, Inspections, Marketing Practices), Department Of Agriculture
description: Code of Federal Regulations, Title 7 (Agriculture), Part 29 (Tobacco Inspection). The percentages shall govern the portion of a lot which must meet the specifications of the grade. (These percentages shall not affect limitations established by other rules.) The minor portion must be closely related.

description: Code of Federal Regulations, Title 7 (Agriculture), Part 29 (Tobacco Inspection). The application of injury tolerance as an element of quality shall be expressed in terms of a percentage. The appraisal of injury shall be based upon the percentage of affected leaf surface or the degree of injury. In appraising injury, consideration shall be given.

creator: Agricultural Marketing Service (Standards, Inspections, Marketing Practices), Department Of Agriculture
description: Code of Federal Regulations, Title 7 (Agriculture), Part 29 (Tobacco Inspection). Text from the eCFR as of 2026-10-26 (unofficial editorial compilation; the official edition is the annual CFR). description: United States law. Code of Federal Regulations, Title 7 (Agriculture), Part 29 (Tobacco Inspection). Text from the eCFR as of 2026-10-26 (unofficial editorial compilation; the official edition is the annual CFR). Damaged under 20 percent. (See Rule 20, § 29.2636.).

title: 7 C.F.R. § 29.2569 — Unstemmed.
creator: Agricultural Marketing Service (Standards, Inspections, Marketing Practices), Department Of Agriculture
description: Code of Federal Regulations, Title 7 (Agriculture), Part 29 (Tobacco Inspection). Text from the eCFR as of 2026-10-26 (unofficial editorial compilation; the official edition is the annual CFR). A form of tobacco, including whole leaf and leaf scrap, from which the stems or midribs have not been removed.

title: 7 C.F.R. § 29.2570 — Wet (W).
creator: Agricultural Marketing Service (Standards, Inspections, Marketing Practices), Department Of Agriculture
description: Code of Federal Regulations, Title 7 (Agriculture), Part 29 (Tobacco Inspection). Text from the eCFR as of 2026-10-26 (unofficial editorial compilation; the official edition is the annual CFR). Any sound tobacco containing excessive moisture to the extent that it is in unsafe or doubtful-keeping order. Wet applies to any tobacco which is not damaged but which is likely to damage if treated in the customary manner. (See Rule 21, § 29.2637.) (For.

title: 7 C.F.R. § 29.2571 — Width.
creator: Agricultural Marketing Service (Standards, Inspections, Marketing Practices), Department Of Agriculture
description: Code of Federal Regulations, Title 7 (Agriculture), Part 29 (Tobacco Inspection). Text from the eCFR as of 2026-10-26 (unofficial editorial compilation; the official edition is the annual CFR). The relative breadth of a tobacco leaf expressed in relation to its length. Width, as an element of quality, does not apply to tobacco in strip form. (See chart, § 29.2601.).

title: 7 C.F.R. § 29.2601 — Elements of quality and degrees of each element.
creator: Agricultural Marketing Service (Standards, Inspections, Marketing Practices), Department Of Agriculture
description: Code of Federal Regulations, Title 7 (Agriculture), Part 29 (Tobacco Inspection). Text from the eCFR as of 2026-10-26 (unofficial editorial compilation; the official edition is the annual CFR). Tobacco attributes or characteristics which constitute quality are designated as elements of quality. The range within each element is expressed by words or terms designated as degrees. These degrees are arranged to show their relative value and are used in determining the quality of.

title: 7 C.F.R. § 29.2616 — Rules.
creator: Agricultural Marketing Service (Standards, Inspections, Marketing Practices), Department Of Agriculture
description: Code of Federal Regulations, Title 7 (Agriculture), Part 29 (Tobacco Inspection). Text from the eCFR as of 2026-10-26 (unofficial editorial compilation; the official edition is the annual CFR). The application of these official standard grades shall be in accordance with §§ 29.2617 through 29.2639.

title: 7 C.F.R. § 29.2617 — Rule 1.
creator: Agricultural Marketing Service (Standards, Inspections, Marketing Practices), Department Of Agriculture
description: Code of Federal Regulations, Title 7 (Agriculture), Part 29 (Tobacco Inspection). Text from the eCFR as of 2026-10-26 (unofficial editorial compilation; the official edition is the annual CFR). Each grade shall be treated as a subdivision of a particular type. When the grade is stated in an inspection certificate, the type also shall be stated.

title: 7 C.F.R. § 29.2618 — Rule 2.
creator: Agricultural Marketing Service (Standards, Inspections, Marketing Practices), Department Of Agriculture
description: Code of Federal Regulations, Title 7 (Agriculture), Part 29 (Tobacco Inspection). Text from the eCFR as of 2026-10-26 (unofficial editorial compilation; the official edition is the annual CFR). The determination of a grade shall be based upon a thorough examination of a lot of tobacco or of an official sample of the lot.

title: 7 C.F.R. § 29.2619 — Rule 3.
creator: Agricultural Marketing Service (Standards, Inspections, Marketing Practices), Department Of Agriculture
description: Code of Federal Regulations, Title 7 (Agriculture), Part 29 (Tobacco Inspection). Text from the eCFR as of 2026-10-26 (unofficial editorial compilation; the official edition is the annual CFR). In drawing an official sample from a hogshead or other package of tobacco, two or more breaks shall be made at such points and in such manner as the inspector or sampler may find necessary to determine the kinds of tobacco and the percentage.

title: 7 C.F.R. § 29.2621 — Rule 5.
creator: Agricultural Marketing Service (Standards, Inspections, Marketing Practices), Department Of Agriculture
description: Code of Federal Regulations, Title 7 (Agriculture), Part 29 (Tobacco Inspection). Text from the eCFR as of 2026-10-26 (unofficial editorial compilation; the official edition is the annual CFR). The grade assigned to any lot of tobacco shall be a true representation of the tobacco at the time of inspection and certification. If, at any time, it is found that a lot of tobacco does not comply with the specifications of the grade.

title: 7 C.F.R. § 29.2622 — Rule 6.
creator: Agricultural Marketing Service (Standards, Inspections, Marketing Practices), Department Of Agriculture
description: Code of Federal Regulations, Title 7 (Agriculture), Part 29 (Tobacco Inspection). Text from the eCFR as of 2026-10-26 (unofficial editorial compilation; the official edition is the annual CFR). A lot of tobacco on the marginal line between two colors shall be placed in the color with which it best corresponds with respect to body or other associated elements of quality.

title: 7 C.F.R. § 29.2623 — Rule 7.
creator: Agricultural Marketing Service (Standards, Inspections, Marketing Practices), Department Of Agriculture
description: Code of Federal Regulations, Title 7 (Agriculture), Part 29 (Tobacco Inspection). Text from the eCFR as of 2026-10-26 (unofficial editorial compilation; the official edition is the annual CFR). Any lot of tobacco which meets the specifications of two grades shall be placed in the higher grade. Any lot of tobacco on the marginal line between two grades shall be placed in the lower grade.

title: 7 C.F.R. § 29.2624 — Rule 8.
creator: Agricultural Marketing Service (Standards, Inspections, Marketing Practices), Department Of Agriculture
description: Code of Federal Regulations, Title 7 (Agriculture), Part 29 (Tobacco Inspection). Text from the eCFR as of 2026-10-26 (unofficial editorial compilation; the official edition is the annual CFR). A lot of tobacco meets the specifications of a grade when it is not lower in any degree of any element of quality than the minimum specifications of such grade.

title: 7 C.F.R. § 29.2625 — Rule 9.
creator: Agricultural Marketing Service (Standards, Inspections, Marketing Practices), Department Of Agriculture
description: Code of Federal Regulations, Title 7 (Agriculture), Part 29 (Tobacco Inspection). Text from the eCFR as of 2026-10-26 (unofficial editorial compilation; the official edition is the annual CFR). In determining the grade of a lot of tobacco, the lot as a whole shall be considered. Minor irregularities which do not affect over one percent of the tobacco shall be overlooked.

title: 7 C.F.R. § 29.2626 — Rule 10.
creator: Agricultural Marketing Service (Standards, Inspections, Marketing Practices), Department Of Agriculture
description: Code of Federal Regulations, Title 7 (Agriculture), Part 29 (Tobacco Inspection). Text from the eCFR as of 2026-10-26 (unofficial editorial compilation; the official edition is the annual CFR). Any special factor approved by the Director of the Tobacco Division, Agricultural Marketing Service, may be used to show a peculiar side or characteristic of the tobacco which tends to modify the grade.

title: 7 C.F.R. § 29.2627 — Rule 11.
creator: Agricultural Marketing Service (Standards, Inspections, Marketing Practices), Department Of Agriculture
description: Code of Federal Regulations, Title 7 (Agriculture), Part 29 (Tobacco Inspection). Text from the eCFR as of 2026-10-26 (unofficial editorial compilation; the official edition is the annual CFR). Interpretations, the use of specifications, and the meaning of terms shall be in accordance with determinations or clarifications made by the Chief of the Standards and Testing Branch and approved by the Director.

title: 7 C.F.R. § 29.2628 — Rule 12.
creator: Agricultural Marketing Service (Standards, Inspections, Marketing Practices), Department Of Agriculture
description: Code of Federal Regulations, Title 7 (Agriculture), Part 29 (Tobacco Inspection). Text from the eCFR as of 2026-10-26 (unofficial editorial compilation; the official edition is the annual CFR). The use of any grade may be restricted by the Director during any marketing season, when it is found that the grade is not needed or appears in insufficient volume to justify its use.

title: 7 C.F.R. § 29.2629 — Rule 13.
creator: Agricultural Marketing Service (Standards, Inspections, Marketing Practices), Department Of Agriculture
description: Code of Federal Regulations, Title 7 (Agriculture), Part 29 (Tobacco Inspection). Text from the eCFR as of 2026-10-26 (unofficial editorial compilation; the official edition is the annual CFR). Length shall be stated in connection with each grade of the A, B, and C groups, except strip grades, and may be stated in connection with the grades of other groups. The standard tobacco sizes shall be used.

title: 7 C.F.R. § 29.2630 — Rule 14.
creator: Agricultural Marketing Service (Standards, Inspections, Marketing Practices), Department Of Agriculture
description: Code of Federal Regulations, Title 7 (Agriculture), Part 29 (Tobacco Inspection). Text from the eCFR as of 2026-10-26 (unofficial editorial compilation; the official edition is the annual CFR). Uniformity shall be expressed in percentages. These percentages shall govern the portion of a lot which must meet each specification of the grade. The minor portion must be closely related but may be of a different group, quality, and color from the major portion.

title: 7 C.F.R. § 29.2631 — Rule 15.
creator: Agricultural Marketing Service (Standards, Inspections, Marketing Practices), Department Of Agriculture
description: Code of Federal Regulations, Title 7 (Agriculture), Part 29 (Tobacco Inspection). Text from the eCFR as of 2026-10-26 (unofficial editorial compilation; the official edition is the annual CFR). Injury tolerance shall be expressed in percentages. The appraisal of injury shall be based upon the percentage of affected leaf surface or the degree of injury. In appraising injury, consideration shall be given to the normal characteristics of the group.

title: 7 C.F.R. § 29.2632 — Rule 16.
creator: Agricultural Marketing Service (Standards, Inspections, Marketing Practices), Department Of Agriculture
description: Code of Federal Regulations, Title 7 (Agriculture), Part 29 (Tobacco Inspection). Text from the eCFR as of 2026-10-26 (unofficial editorial compilation; the official edition is the annual CFR). Any lot of tobacco of the B, C, or X groups containing over 30 percent of mixed color or variegated leaves or over 30 percent of mixed color and variegated leaves combined shall be classified as “mixed” and designated by the color symbol “M.”.

title: 7 C.F.R. § 29.2633 — Rule 17.
creator: Agricultural Marketing Service (Standards, Inspections, Marketing Practices), Department Of Agriculture
description: Code of Federal Regulations, Title 7 (Agriculture), Part 29 (Tobacco Inspection). Text from the eCFR as of 2026-10-26 (unofficial editorial compilation; the official edition is the annual CFR). Any lot of tobacco containing 20 percent or more of greenish leaves or any lot which contains 20 percent of greenish and green leaves combined shall be designated by the color symbol “VF.”.

title: 7 C.F.R. § 29.2634 — Rule 18.
creator: Agricultural Marketing Service (Standards, Inspections, Marketing Practices), Department Of Agriculture
description: Code of Federal Regulations, Title 7 (Agriculture), Part 29 (Tobacco Inspection). Text from the eCFR as of 2026-10-26 (unofficial editorial compilation; the official edition is the annual CFR). Any lot of tobacco containing 20 percent or more of green leaves or any lot which is not crude but contains 20 percent or more of green and crude combined shall be designated by the color symbol “G.”.

title: 7 C.F.R. § 29.2635 — Rule 19.
creator: Agricultural Marketing Service (Standards, Inspections, Marketing Practices), Department Of Agriculture
description: Code of Federal Regulations, Title 7 (Agriculture), Part 29 (Tobacco Inspection). Text from the eCFR as of 2026-10-26 (unofficial editorial compilation; the official edition is the annual CFR). In the B, C, and X groups crude leaves shall be restricted to the fourth and fifth qualities of green grades. Any lot containing 20 percent or more of crude leaves shall be classified as Nondescript.

title: 7 C.F.R. § 29.2636 — Rule 20.
creator: Agricultural Marketing Service (Standards, Inspections, Marketing Practices), Department Of Agriculture
description: Code of Federal Regulations, Title 7 (Agriculture), Part 29 (Tobacco Inspection). Text from the eCFR as of 2026-10-26 (unofficial editorial compilation; the official edition is the annual CFR). Tobacco damaged under 20 percent but which otherwise meets the specifications of a grade shall be treated as a subgrade by placing the special factor “U” after the grademark. Tobacco damaged 20 percent or more shall be designated “No-G.”.

title: 7 C.F.R. § 29.2637 — Rule 21.
creator: Agricultural Marketing Service (Standards, Inspections, Marketing Practices), Department Of Agriculture
description: Code of Federal Regulations, Title 7 (Agriculture), Part 29 (Tobacco Inspection). Text from the eCFR as of 2026-10-26 (unofficial editorial compilation; the official edition is the annual CFR). Sound tobacco that is wet or in doubtful-keeping order but which otherwise meets the specifications of a grade shall be treated as a subgrade by placing the special factor “W” after the grademark. This special factor does not apply to tobacco designated “No-G.”.

title: 7 C.F.R. § 29.2638 — Rule 22.
creator: Agricultural Marketing Service (Standards, Inspections, Marketing Practices), Department Of Agriculture
description: Code of Federal Regulations, Title 7 (Agriculture), Part 29 (Tobacco Inspection). Text from the eCFR as of 2026-10-26 (unofficial editorial compilation; the official edition is the annual CFR). Tobacco shall be designated No Grade, using the grademark “No-G,” when it is dirty, nested, offtype, semicured, damaged 20 percent or more, extremely wet or watered, or when it needs to be reworked, contains foreign matter, or has an odor foreign to type.

title: 7 C.F.R. § 29.2639 — Rule 23.
creator: Agricultural Marketing Service (Standards, Inspections, Marketing Practices), Department Of Agriculture
description: Code of Federal Regulations, Title 7 (Agriculture), Part 29 (Tobacco Inspection). Text from the eCFR as of 2026-10-26 (unofficial editorial compilation; the official edition is the annual CFR). Tobacco in strip form which otherwise meets the specifications of a grade shall be treated as a subgrade by placing the special factor “S” preceding the grademark.

title: 7 C.F.R. § 29.2640 — Rule 24.
creator: Agricultural Marketing Service (Standards, Inspections, Marketing Practices), Department Of Agriculture
description: Code of Federal Regulations, Title 7 (Agriculture), Part 29 (Tobacco Inspection). Text from the eCFR as of 2026-10-26 (unofficial editorial compilation; the official edition is the annual CFR). Tobacco that is semifired but which otherwise meets the specifications of a grade shall be treated as a subgrade by placing the special factor “SF” after the grademark. This factor does not apply to tobacco designated “No-G”.

title: 7 C.F.R. § 29.2661 — Wrappers (A Group).
creator: Agricultural Marketing Service (Standards, Inspections, Marketing Practices), Department Of Agriculture
description: Code of Federal Regulations, Title 7 (Agriculture), Part 29 (Tobacco Inspection). Text from the eCFR as of 2026-10-26 (unofficial editorial compilation; the official edition is the annual CFR). This group consists of leaves usually grown at or above the center portion of the stalk. Cured leaves of this group are elastic and show a low percentage of injury affecting wrapper yield.

title: 7 C.F.R. § 29.2662 — Heavy Leaf (B Group).
creator: Agricultural Marketing Service (Standards, Inspections, Marketing Practices), Department Of Agriculture
description: Code of Federal Regulations, Title 7 (Agriculture), Part 29 (Tobacco Inspection). Text from the eCFR as of 2026-10-26 (unofficial editorial compilation; the official edition is the annual CFR). This group consists of leaves which are medium to heavy in body.

title: 7 C.F.R. § 29.2663 — Thin Leaf (C Group).
creator: Agricultural Marketing Service (Standards, Inspections, Marketing Practices), Department Of Agriculture
description: United States law. Code of Federal Regulations, Title 7 (Agriculture), Part 29 (Tobacco Inspection). Text from the eCFR as of 2026-10-26 (unofficial editorial compilation; the official edition is the annual CFR). This group consists of leaves that are thin in body.

title: 7 C.F.R. § 29.2664 — Lugs (X Group).
creator: Agricultural Marketing Service (Standards, Inspections, Marketing Practices), Department Of Agriculture
description: Code of Federal Regulations, Title 7 (Agriculture), Part 29 (Tobacco Inspection). Text from the eCFR as of 2026-10-26 (unofficial editorial compilation; the official edition is the annual CFR). This group consists of leaves that normally grow near the bottom of the stalk. Leaves of the X group usually have a high degree of maturity and show ground injury.

title: 7 C.F.R. § 29.2665 — Nondescript (N Group).
creator: Agricultural Marketing Service (Standards, Inspections, Marketing Practices), Department Of Agriculture
description: Code of Federal Regulations, Title 7 (Agriculture), Part 29 (Tobacco Inspection). Text from the eCFR as of 2026-10-26 (unofficial editorial compilation; the official edition is the annual CFR). Extremely common tobacco which does not meet the minimum specifications or which exceeds the tolerance of the lowest grade of any other group except Scrap.

title: 7 C.F.R. § 29.2666 — Scrap (S Group).
creator: Agricultural Marketing Service (Standards, Inspections, Marketing Practices), Department Of Agriculture
description: Code of Federal Regulations, Title 7 (Agriculture), Part 29 (Tobacco Inspection). Text from the eCFR as of 2026-10-26 (unofficial editorial compilation; the official edition is the annual CFR). A byproduct of unstemmed and stemmed tobacco. Scrap accumulates from handling tobacco in farm buildings, warehouses, packing and conditioning plants, and stemmeries.

title: 7 C.F.R. § 29.3001 — Definitions.
creator: Agricultural Marketing Service (Standards, Inspections, Marketing Practices), Department Of Agriculture
description: Code of Federal Regulations, Title 7 (Agriculture), Part 29 (Tobacco Inspection). Text from the eCFR as of 2026-10-26 (unofficial editorial compilation; the official edition is the annual CFR). As used in these standards, the words and phrases hereinafter defined shall have the indicated meanings so assigned.

title: 7 C.F.R. § 29.3002 — Air-cured.
creator: Agricultural Marketing Service (Standards, Inspections, Marketing Practices), Department Of Agriculture
description: Code of Federal Regulations, Title 7 (Agriculture), Part 29 (Tobacco Inspection). Text from the eCFR as of 2026-10-26 (unofficial editorial compilation; the official edition is the annual CFR). Tobacco cured under natural atmospheric conditions. Artificial heat is sometimes used to control excess humidity during the curing period to prevent house-burn and barn-burn in damp weather. Air-cured tobacco should not carry the odor of smoke or fumes resulting from the application of artificial.

title: 7 C.F.R. § 29.3003 — Air-dried.
creator: Agricultural Marketing Service (Standards, Inspections, Marketing Practices), Department Of Agriculture
description: Code of Federal Regulations, Title 7 (Agriculture), Part 29 (Tobacco Inspection). Text from the eCFR as of 2026-10-26 (unofficial editorial compilation; the official edition is the annual CFR). The condition of unfermented tobacco as customarily prepared for storage under natural atmospheric conditions.

title: 7 C.F.R. § 29.3004 — Body.
creator: Agricultural Marketing Service (Standards, Inspections, Marketing Practices), Department Of Agriculture
description: Code of Federal Regulations, Title 7 (Agriculture), Part 29 (Tobacco Inspection). Text from the eCFR as of 2026-10-26 (unofficial editorial compilation; the official edition is the annual CFR). The thickness and density of a leaf or the weight per unit of surface. (See Elements of quality.).

title: 7 C.F.R. § 29.3005 — Burley, Type 31.
creator: Agricultural Marketing Service (Standards, Inspections, Marketing Practices), Department Of Agriculture
description: Code of Federal Regulations, Title 7 (Agriculture), Part 29 (Tobacco Inspection). Text from the eCFR as of 2026-10-26 (unofficial editorial compilation; the official edition is the annual CFR). That type of air-cured tobacco, commonly known as Burley, produced principally in Kentucky, Tennessee, Virginia, North Carolina, Ohio, Indiana, West Virginia, and Missouri.

title: 7 C.F.R. § 29.3006 — Burley, Type 93.
creator: Agricultural Marketing Service (Standards, Inspections, Marketing Practices), Department Of Agriculture
description: Code of Federal Regulations, Title 7 (Agriculture), Part 29 (Tobacco Inspection). Text from the eCFR as of 2026-10-26 (unofficial editorial compilation; the official edition is the annual CFR). That type of air-cured tobacco commonly known as Foreign-grown Burley, produced in countries other than the United States.

title: 7 C.F.R. § 29.3008 — Class.
creator: Agricultural Marketing Service (Standards, Inspections, Marketing Practices), Department Of Agriculture
description: Code of Federal Regulations, Title 7 (Agriculture), Part 29 (Tobacco Inspection). Text from the eCFR as of 2026-10-26 (unofficial editorial compilation; the official edition is the annual CFR). A major division of tobacco based on method of cure or principal usage.

title: 7 C.F.R. § 29.3009 — Clean.
creator: Agricultural Marketing Service (Standards, Inspections, Marketing Practices), Department Of Agriculture
description: Code of Federal Regulations, Title 7 (Agriculture), Part 29 (Tobacco Inspection). Text from the eCFR as of 2026-10-26 (unofficial editorial compilation; the official edition is the annual CFR). Tobacco is described as clean when it contains only a normal amount of sand or soil particles. Leaves grown on the lower portion of the stalk normally contain more dirt or sand than those from higher stalk positions. (See Rule 20.).

title: 7 C.F.R. § 29.3010 — Color.
creator: Agricultural Marketing Service (Standards, Inspections, Marketing Practices), Department Of Agriculture
description: Code of Federal Regulations, Title 7 (Agriculture), Part 29 (Tobacco Inspection). Text from the eCFR as of 2026-10-26 (unofficial editorial compilation; the official edition is the annual CFR). The third factor of a grade, based on the relative hues, saturations or chroma, and color values common to the type.

title: 7 C.F.R. § 29.3011 — Color intensity.
creator: Agricultural Marketing Service (Standards, Inspections, Marketing Practices), Department Of Agriculture
description: Code of Federal Regulations, Title 7 (Agriculture), Part 29 (Tobacco Inspection). Text from the eCFR as of 2026-10-26 (unofficial editorial compilation; the official edition is the annual CFR). The varying degree of saturation or chroma. Color intensity as applied to tobacco describes the strength or weakness of a specific color or hue. It is applicable to all colors except variegated. Color intensity is reversed in its application to grades of greenish and.

title: 7 C.F.R. § 29.3012 — Color symbols.
creator: Agricultural Marketing Service (Standards, Inspections, Marketing Practices), Department Of Agriculture
description: Code of Federal Regulations, Title 7 (Agriculture), Part 29 (Tobacco Inspection). Text from the eCFR as of 2026-10-26 (unofficial editorial compilation; the official edition is the annual CFR). As applied to Burley, single color symbols are as follows: L—buff, F—tan, R—red, D—dark red, K—variegated, M—mixed color, V—greenish, and G—green.

title: 7 C.F.R. § 29.3013 — Combination color symbols.
creator: Agricultural Marketing Service (Standards, Inspections, Marketing Practices), Department Of Agriculture
description: Code of Federal Regulations, Title 7 (Agriculture), Part 29 (Tobacco Inspection). Text from the eCFR as of 2026-10-26 (unofficial editorial compilation; the official edition is the annual CFR). As applied to Burley, combination color symbols are as follows: FL—tannish buff, FR—tannish red, VF—greenish tan, VR—greenish red, GF—green tan, and GR—green red. (See rules 17 and 18.).

title: 7 C.F.R. § 29.3014 — Condition.
creator: Agricultural Marketing Service (Standards, Inspections, Marketing Practices), Department Of Agriculture
description: Code of Federal Regulations, Title 7 (Agriculture), Part 29 (Tobacco Inspection). Text from the eCFR as of 2026-10-26 (unofficial editorial compilation; the official edition is the annual CFR). The state of tobacco which results from the method of preparation or from the degree of fermentation. Words used to describe the condition of tobacco are as follows: Undried, air-dried, steam-dried, sweating, sweated, and aged. Burley is air-dried or steam-dried for storage and aging.

title: 7 C.F.R. § 29.3015 — Crude.
creator: Agricultural Marketing Service (Standards, Inspections, Marketing Practices), Department Of Agriculture
description: Code of Federal Regulations, Title 7 (Agriculture), Part 29 (Tobacco Inspection). Text from the eCFR as of 2026-10-26 (unofficial editorial compilation; the official edition is the annual CFR). A subdegree of maturity. Crude leaves are usually hard and slick as a result of extreme immaturity. A similar condition may result from sunburn or sunscald. Any leaf which is crude to the extent of 20 percent of its leaf surface may be described.

title: 7 C.F.R. § 29.3016 — Cured.
creator: Agricultural Marketing Service (Standards, Inspections, Marketing Practices), Department Of Agriculture
description: United States law. Code of Federal Regulations, Title 7 (Agriculture), Part 29 (Tobacco Inspection). Text from the eCFR as of 2026-10-26 (unofficial editorial compilation; the official edition is the annual CFR). Tobacco dried of its sap by either natural or artificial processes.

title: 7 C.F.R. § 29.3017 — Damage.
creator: Agricultural Marketing Service (Standards, Inspections, Marketing Practices), Department Of Agriculture
description: Code of Federal Regulations, Title 7 (Agriculture), Part 29 (Tobacco Inspection). Text from the eCFR as of 2026-10-26 (unofficial editorial compilation; the official edition is the annual CFR). The effect of mold, must, rot, black rot, or other fungous or bacterial diseases which attack tobacco in its cured state. Tobacco having the odor of mold, must, or rot is considered damaged. (See Rule 23.).

title: 7 C.F.R. § 29.3019 — Dirty.
creator: Agricultural Marketing Service (Standards, Inspections, Marketing Practices), Department Of Agriculture
description: Code of Federal Regulations, Title 7 (Agriculture), Part 29 (Tobacco Inspection). Text from the eCFR as of 2026-10-26 (unofficial editorial compilation; the official edition is the annual CFR). The state of tobacco containing an abnormal amount of dirt or sand, or tobacco to which additional quantities of dirt or sand have been added. (See Rule 23.).

title: 7 C.F.R. § 29.3020 — Elements of quality.
creator: Agricultural Marketing Service (Standards, Inspections, Marketing Practices), Department Of Agriculture
description: Code of Federal Regulations, Title 7 (Agriculture), Part 29 (Tobacco Inspection). Text from the eCFR as of 2026-10-26 (unofficial editorial compilation; the official edition is the annual CFR). Elements of quality and the degrees used in the specifications of the official standard grades of Burley, Types 31 and 93, are shown in § 29.3101. Words have been selected to describe the degrees of each element. Some of the words are almost synonymous.

title: 7 C.F.R. § 29.3021 — Fiber.
creator: Agricultural Marketing Service (Standards, Inspections, Marketing Practices), Department Of Agriculture
description: Code of Federal Regulations, Title 7 (Agriculture), Part 29 (Tobacco Inspection). Text from the eCFR as of 2026-10-26 (unofficial editorial compilation; the official edition is the annual CFR). The term applied to the veins in a tobacco leaf. The large central vein is called the midrib or stem. The smaller lateral and cross veins are considered from the standpoint of size and color and in some types are treated as elements of.

title: 7 C.F.R. § 29.3022 — Finish.
creator: Agricultural Marketing Service (Standards, Inspections, Marketing Practices), Department Of Agriculture
description: Code of Federal Regulations, Title 7 (Agriculture), Part 29 (Tobacco Inspection). Text from the eCFR as of 2026-10-26 (unofficial editorial compilation; the official edition is the annual CFR). The reflectance factor in color perception. Finish indicates the sheen or shine of the surface of a tobacco leaf. Descriptive terms range from bright to dingy. (See Elements of quality.).

title: 7 C.F.R. § 29.3023 — Foreign matter.
creator: Agricultural Marketing Service (Standards, Inspections, Marketing Practices), Department Of Agriculture
description: Code of Federal Regulations, Title 7 (Agriculture), Part 29 (Tobacco Inspection). Text from the eCFR as of 2026-10-26 (unofficial editorial compilation; the official edition is the annual CFR). Any extraneous substance or material such as stalks, suckers, straw, strings, rubber bands, et cetera. Abnormal amounts of dirt or sand also are included. (See Rule 23.).

title: 7 C.F.R. § 29.3024 — Form.
creator: Agricultural Marketing Service (Standards, Inspections, Marketing Practices), Department Of Agriculture
description: United States law. Code of Federal Regulations, Title 7 (Agriculture), Part 29 (Tobacco Inspection). Text from the eCFR as of 2026-10-26 (unofficial editorial compilation; the official edition is the annual CFR). The stage of preparation of tobacco such as unstemmed or stemmed.

title: 7 C.F.R. § 29.3025 — General color.
creator: Agricultural Marketing Service (Standards, Inspections, Marketing Practices), Department Of Agriculture
description: Code of Federal Regulations, Title 7 (Agriculture), Part 29 (Tobacco Inspection). Text from the eCFR as of 2026-10-26 (unofficial editorial compilation; the official edition is the annual CFR). The color of tobacco considered in relation to the type as a whole. General color is distinguished from the restricted use of the term “color” within a group. It is basically related to body and other overall characteristics of the type.

title: 7 C.F.R. § 29.3026 — General quality.
creator: Agricultural Marketing Service (Standards, Inspections, Marketing Practices), Department Of Agriculture
description: Code of Federal Regulations, Title 7 (Agriculture), Part 29 (Tobacco Inspection). Text from the eCFR as of 2026-10-26 (unofficial editorial compilation; the official edition is the annual CFR). The quality of tobacco considered in relation to the type as a whole. General quality is distinguished from the restricted use of the term “quality” within a group.

title: 7 C.F.R. § 29.3027 — Grade.
creator: Agricultural Marketing Service (Standards, Inspections, Marketing Practices), Department Of Agriculture
description: United States law. Code of Federal Regulations, Title 7 (Agriculture), Part 29 (Tobacco Inspection). Text from the eCFR as of 2026-10-26 (unofficial editorial compilation; the official edition is the annual CFR). A subdivision of a type according to group, quality, and color.

title: 7 C.F.R. § 29.3028 — Grademark.
creator: Agricultural Marketing Service (Standards, Inspections, Marketing Practices), Department Of Agriculture
description: Code of Federal Regulations, Title 7 (Agriculture), Part 29 (Tobacco Inspection). Text from the eCFR as of 2026-10-26 (unofficial editorial compilation; the official edition is the annual CFR). A grademark normally consists of three symbols which indicate group, quality, and color. A letter is used to indicate group, a number to indicate quality, and a letter or letters to indicate color. For example, C2F means Lugs, second quality, and tan color.

title: 7 C.F.R. § 29.3029 — Green (G).
creator: Agricultural Marketing Service (Standards, Inspections, Marketing Practices), Department Of Agriculture
description: Code of Federal Regulations, Title 7 (Agriculture), Part 29 (Tobacco Inspection). Text from the eCFR as of 2026-10-26 (unofficial editorial compilation; the official edition is the annual CFR). A color term applied to immature or crude tobacco. Any leaf which has a green color affecting 20 percent or more of its leaf surface may be described as green. (See Rule 18.).

title: 7 C.F.R. § 29.3030 — Greenish (V).
creator: Agricultural Marketing Service (Standards, Inspections, Marketing Practices), Department Of Agriculture
description: Code of Federal Regulations, Title 7 (Agriculture), Part 29 (Tobacco Inspection). Text from the eCFR as of 2026-10-26 (unofficial editorial compilation; the official edition is the annual CFR). A color term applied to greenish-tinged tobacco. Any leaf which has a greenish tinge or a pale green color affecting 20 percent or more of its surface may be described as greenish. (See Rule 17.).

title: 7 C.F.R. § 29.3031 — Group.
creator: Agricultural Marketing Service (Standards, Inspections, Marketing Practices), Department Of Agriculture
description: Code of Federal Regulations, Title 7 (Agriculture), Part 29 (Tobacco Inspection). Text from the eCFR as of 2026-10-26 (unofficial editorial compilation; the official edition is the annual CFR). A division of a type covering closely related grades based on certain characteristics which are related to stalk position or the general quality of the tobacco. Groups in Burley, Types 31 and 93, are as follows: Flyings (X), Lugs or Cutters (C), Leaf (B).

title: 7 C.F.R. § 29.3032 — Injury.
creator: Agricultural Marketing Service (Standards, Inspections, Marketing Practices), Department Of Agriculture
description: Code of Federal Regulations, Title 7 (Agriculture), Part 29 (Tobacco Inspection). Text from the eCFR as of 2026-10-26 (unofficial editorial compilation; the official edition is the annual CFR). Hurt or impairment from any cause except the fungous or bacterial diseases which attack tobacco in its cured state. (See definition of Damage.) Injury to tobacco may be caused by field diseases, insects, or weather conditions; insecticides, fungicides, or cell growth inhibitors; nutritional deficiencies.

title: 7 C.F.R. § 29.3033 — Leaf.
creator: Agricultural Marketing Service (Standards, Inspections, Marketing Practices), Department Of Agriculture
description: Code of Federal Regulations, Title 7 (Agriculture), Part 29 (Tobacco Inspection). Text from the eCFR as of 2026-10-26 (unofficial editorial compilation; the official edition is the annual CFR). Whole, unstemmed leaf. Leaf, when applied to tobacco in strip form, shall describe the divided unit of a whole leaf.

title: 7 C.F.R. § 29.3034 — Leaf scrap.
creator: Agricultural Marketing Service (Standards, Inspections, Marketing Practices), Department Of Agriculture
description: Code of Federal Regulations, Title 7 (Agriculture), Part 29 (Tobacco Inspection). Text from the eCFR as of 2026-10-26 (unofficial editorial compilation; the official edition is the annual CFR). A by-product of unstemmed tobacco. Leaf scrap results from handling unstemmed tobacco and consists of loose and tangled whole or broken leaves.

title: 7 C.F.R. § 29.3035 — Leaf structure.
creator: Agricultural Marketing Service (Standards, Inspections, Marketing Practices), Department Of Agriculture
description: Code of Federal Regulations, Title 7 (Agriculture), Part 29 (Tobacco Inspection). Text from the eCFR as of 2026-10-26 (unofficial editorial compilation; the official edition is the annual CFR). The cell development of a leaf as indicated by its porosity or solidity. (See Elements of quality.).

title: 7 C.F.R. § 29.3036 — Leaf surface.
creator: Agricultural Marketing Service (Standards, Inspections, Marketing Practices), Department Of Agriculture
description: Code of Federal Regulations, Title 7 (Agriculture), Part 29 (Tobacco Inspection). Text from the eCFR as of 2026-10-26 (unofficial editorial compilation; the official edition is the annual CFR). The smoothness or roughness of the web or lamina of a tobacco leaf. Leaf surface is affected to some extent by the size and shrinkage of the veins or fibers. (See Elements of quality.).

title: 7 C.F.R. § 29.3037 — Length.
creator: Agricultural Marketing Service (Standards, Inspections, Marketing Practices), Department Of Agriculture
description: Code of Federal Regulations, Title 7 (Agriculture), Part 29 (Tobacco Inspection). Text from the eCFR as of 2026-10-26 (unofficial editorial compilation; the official edition is the annual CFR). The linear measurement of cured tobacco leaves from the butt of the midrib to the extreme tip. Length, as an element of quality, does not apply to tobacco in strip form. (See Elements of quality.).

title: 7 C.F.R. § 29.3038 — Lot.
creator: Agricultural Marketing Service (Standards, Inspections, Marketing Practices), Department Of Agriculture
description: Code of Federal Regulations, Title 7 (Agriculture), Part 29 (Tobacco Inspection). Text from the eCFR as of 2026-10-26 (unofficial editorial compilation; the official edition is the annual CFR). A pile, basket, bulk, bale or bales, sheet, case hogshead, tierce, package, or other definite package unit.

title: 7 C.F.R. § 29.3039 — Maturity.
creator: Agricultural Marketing Service (Standards, Inspections, Marketing Practices), Department Of Agriculture
description: Code of Federal Regulations, Title 7 (Agriculture), Part 29 (Tobacco Inspection). Text from the eCFR as of 2026-10-26 (unofficial editorial compilation; the official edition is the annual CFR). The degree of ripeness. Tobacco is mature when it reaches its prime state of development. The extremes are expressed as immature and mellow. (See Elements of quality.).

title: 7 C.F.R. § 29.3040 — Mixed color (M).
creator: Agricultural Marketing Service (Standards, Inspections, Marketing Practices), Department Of Agriculture
description: United States law. Code of Federal Regulations, Title 7 (Agriculture), Part 29 (Tobacco Inspection). Text from the eCFR as of 2026-10-26 (unofficial editorial compilation; the official edition is the annual CFR). Distinctly different colors of the type mingled together. (See Rule 16.).

title: 7 C.F.R. § 29.3041 — Nested.
creator: Agricultural Marketing Service (Standards, Inspections, Marketing Practices), Department Of Agriculture
description: Code of Federal Regulations, Title 7 (Agriculture), Part 29 (Tobacco Inspection). Text from the eCFR as of 2026-10-26 (unofficial editorial compilation; the official edition is the annual CFR). Any lot of Type 31 tobacco which as has been loaded, packed or arranged to conceal foreign matter or tobacco of inferior grade, quality, or condition. Nested includes: (a) Any lot of tobacco which contains foreign matter, is damaged, injured, or tangled, or contains.

title: 7 C.F.R. § 29.3042 — No grade.
creator: Agricultural Marketing Service (Standards, Inspections, Marketing Practices), Department Of Agriculture
description: Code of Federal Regulations, Title 7 (Agriculture), Part 29 (Tobacco Inspection). Text from the eCFR as of 2026-10-26 (unofficial editorial compilation; the official edition is the annual CFR). A designation applied to a lot of tobacco which is classified as offtype, rework, semicured, damaged 20 percent or more, abnormally dirty, contains foreign matter, and/or having an odor foreign to the type.

title: 7 C.F.R. § 29.3043 — No-G-Nested.
creator: Agricultural Marketing Service (Standards, Inspections, Marketing Practices), Department Of Agriculture
description: Code of Federal Regulations, Title 7 (Agriculture), Part 29 (Tobacco Inspection). Text from the eCFR as of 2026-10-26 (unofficial editorial compilation; the official edition is the annual CFR). A designation applied to a lot of Type 31 tobacco which is classified as nested.

title: 7 C.F.R. § 29.3044 — Offtype.
creator: Agricultural Marketing Service (Standards, Inspections, Marketing Practices), Department Of Agriculture
description: Code of Federal Regulations, Title 7 (Agriculture), Part 29 (Tobacco Inspection). Text from the eCFR as of 2026-10-26 (unofficial editorial compilation; the official edition is the annual CFR). Tobacco of distinctly different characteristics which cannot be classified as Burley, Type 31 or 93. (See Rule 23.).

title: 7 C.F.R. § 29.3045 — Order (case).
creator: Agricultural Marketing Service (Standards, Inspections, Marketing Practices), Department Of Agriculture
description: United States law. Code of Federal Regulations, Title 7 (Agriculture), Part 29 (Tobacco Inspection). Text from the eCFR as of 2026-10-26 (unofficial editorial compilation; the official edition is the annual CFR). The state of tobacco with respect to its moisture content.

title: 7 C.F.R. § 29.3046 — Oriented.
creator: Agricultural Marketing Service (Standards, Inspections, Marketing Practices), Department Of Agriculture
description: Code of Federal Regulations, Title 7 (Agriculture), Part 29 (Tobacco Inspection). Text from the eCFR as of 2026-10-26 (unofficial editorial compilation; the official edition is the annual CFR). A term applied to Type 31 untied tobacco which denotes the arrangement of leaves in a straight and orderly manner. Oriented includes: (a) Any lot of baled tobacco in which the leaves are packed parallel to the length of the bale with the butts.

title: 7 C.F.R. § 29.3047 — Package.
creator: Agricultural Marketing Service (Standards, Inspections, Marketing Practices), Department Of Agriculture
description: Code of Federal Regulations, Title 7 (Agriculture), Part 29 (Tobacco Inspection). Text from the eCFR as of 2026-10-26 (unofficial editorial compilation; the official edition is the annual CFR). A hogshead, tierce, case, bale, or other securely enclosed parcel or bundle.

title: 7 C.F.R. § 29.3048 — Packing.
creator: Agricultural Marketing Service (Standards, Inspections, Marketing Practices), Department Of Agriculture
description: Code of Federal Regulations, Title 7 (Agriculture), Part 29 (Tobacco Inspection). Text from the eCFR as of 2026-10-26 (unofficial editorial compilation; the official edition is the annual CFR). A lot of tobacco consisting of a number of packages submitted as one definite unit for sampling or inspection. It is represented to contain the same kind of tobacco and has a common identification number or mark on each package.

title: 7 C.F.R. § 29.3049 — Pink or pinkish.
creator: Agricultural Marketing Service (Standards, Inspections, Marketing Practices), Department Of Agriculture
description: Code of Federal Regulations, Title 7 (Agriculture), Part 29 (Tobacco Inspection). Text from the eCFR as of 2026-10-26 (unofficial editorial compilation; the official edition is the annual CFR). A color term applied to pink or pinkish tobacco. Any leaf which has a pink or pinkish color affecting 20 percent or more of its leaf surface is considered as mixed color. (See Rule 16.).

title: 7 C.F.R. § 29.3050 — Quality.
creator: Agricultural Marketing Service (Standards, Inspections, Marketing Practices), Department Of Agriculture
description: Code of Federal Regulations, Title 7 (Agriculture), Part 29 (Tobacco Inspection). Text from the eCFR as of 2026-10-26 (unofficial editorial compilation; the official edition is the annual CFR). A division of a group or the second factor of a grade, based on the relative degree of one or more elements of quality in tobacco.

title: 7 C.F.R. § 29.3051 — Raw.
creator: Agricultural Marketing Service (Standards, Inspections, Marketing Practices), Department Of Agriculture
description: Code of Federal Regulations, Title 7 (Agriculture), Part 29 (Tobacco Inspection). Text from the eCFR as of 2026-10-26 (unofficial editorial compilation; the official edition is the annual CFR). Freshly harvested tobacco or tobacco as it appears between the time of harvesting and the beginning of the curing process.

title: 7 C.F.R. § 29.3053 — Rework.
creator: Agricultural Marketing Service (Standards, Inspections, Marketing Practices), Department Of Agriculture
description: Code of Federal Regulations, Title 7 (Agriculture), Part 29 (Tobacco Inspection). Text from the eCFR as of 2026-10-26 (unofficial editorial compilation; the official edition is the annual CFR). Any lot of Type 31 tobacco which needs to be restored or otherwise rearranged to prepare it properly for market, including: (a) Tobacco which contains an abnormally large quantity of foreign matter or an unusual number of muddy or extremely dirty leaves which should.

title: 7 C.F.R. § 29.3054 — Semicured.
creator: Agricultural Marketing Service (Standards, Inspections, Marketing Practices), Department Of Agriculture
description: Code of Federal Regulations, Title 7 (Agriculture), Part 29 (Tobacco Inspection). Text from the eCFR as of 2026-10-26 (unofficial editorial compilation; the official edition is the annual CFR). Tobacco in the process of being cured or which is partially but not thoroughly cured. Semicured includes tobacco which contains fat stems, wet butts, swell stems, frozen tobacco, and tobacco having frozen stems or stems that have not been thoroughly dried in the curing.

title: 7 C.F.R. § 29.3055 — Side.
creator: Agricultural Marketing Service (Standards, Inspections, Marketing Practices), Department Of Agriculture
description: Code of Federal Regulations, Title 7 (Agriculture), Part 29 (Tobacco Inspection). Text from the eCFR as of 2026-10-26 (unofficial editorial compilation; the official edition is the annual CFR). A certain phase of quality, color, or length as contrasted with some other phase of quality, color, or length; or any peculiar characteristic of tobacco.

title: 7 C.F.R. § 29.3057 — Special factor.
creator: Agricultural Marketing Service (Standards, Inspections, Marketing Practices), Department Of Agriculture
description: Code of Federal Regulations, Title 7 (Agriculture), Part 29 (Tobacco Inspection). Text from the eCFR as of 2026-10-26 (unofficial editorial compilation; the official edition is the annual CFR). A symbol or term authorized to be used with specified grades. Tobacco to which a special factor is applied may meet the general specifications but has a peculiar side or characteristic which tends to modify the grade. (See Rule 9.).

title: 7 C.F.R. § 29.3058 — Steam-dried.
creator: Agricultural Marketing Service (Standards, Inspections, Marketing Practices), Department Of Agriculture
description: Code of Federal Regulations, Title 7 (Agriculture), Part 29 (Tobacco Inspection). Text from the eCFR as of 2026-10-26 (unofficial editorial compilation; the official edition is the annual CFR). The condition of unfermented tobacco as customarily prepared for storage by means of a redrying machine or other steam-conditioning equipment.

title: 7 C.F.R. § 29.3059 — Stem.
creator: Agricultural Marketing Service (Standards, Inspections, Marketing Practices), Department Of Agriculture
description: United States law. Code of Federal Regulations, Title 7 (Agriculture), Part 29 (Tobacco Inspection). Text from the eCFR as of 2026-10-26 (unofficial editorial compilation; the official edition is the annual CFR). The midrib or large central vein of a tobacco leaf.

title: 7 C.F.R. § 29.3060 — Stemmed.
creator: Agricultural Marketing Service (Standards, Inspections, Marketing Practices), Department Of Agriculture
description: Code of Federal Regulations, Title 7 (Agriculture), Part 29 (Tobacco Inspection). Text from the eCFR as of 2026-10-26 (unofficial editorial compilation; the official edition is the annual CFR). A form of tobacco, including strips and strip scrap, from which the stems or midribs have been removed.

title: 7 C.F.R. § 29.3061 — Strength (tensile).
creator: Agricultural Marketing Service (Standards, Inspections, Marketing Practices), Department Of Agriculture
description: Code of Federal Regulations, Title 7 (Agriculture), Part 29 (Tobacco Inspection). Text from the eCFR as of 2026-10-26 (unofficial editorial compilation; the official edition is the annual CFR). The stress a tobacco leaf can bear without tearing. Tensile strength is not an important element of quality in Burley tobacco.

title: 7 C.F.R. § 29.3062 — Strips.
creator: Agricultural Marketing Service (Standards, Inspections, Marketing Practices), Department Of Agriculture
description: Code of Federal Regulations, Title 7 (Agriculture), Part 29 (Tobacco Inspection). Text from the eCFR as of 2026-10-26 (unofficial editorial compilation; the official edition is the annual CFR). The sides of a tobacco leaf from which the stem has been removed; or a lot of tobacco composed of strips.

title: 7 C.F.R. § 29.3064 — Sweated.
creator: Agricultural Marketing Service (Standards, Inspections, Marketing Practices), Department Of Agriculture
description: Code of Federal Regulations, Title 7 (Agriculture), Part 29 (Tobacco Inspection). Text from the eCFR as of 2026-10-26 (unofficial editorial compilation; the official edition is the annual CFR). The condition of tobacco which has passed through one or more fermentations natural to tobacco packed with a normal percentage of moisture. This condition is sometimes described as aged.

title: 7 C.F.R. § 29.3065 — Sweating.
creator: Agricultural Marketing Service (Standards, Inspections, Marketing Practices), Department Of Agriculture
description: United States law. Code of Federal Regulations, Title 7 (Agriculture), Part 29 (Tobacco Inspection). Text from the eCFR as of 2026-10-26 (unofficial editorial compilation; the official edition is the annual CFR). The condition of tobacco in the process of fermentation.

title: 7 C.F.R. § 29.3069 — Tobacco.
creator: Agricultural Marketing Service (Standards, Inspections, Marketing Practices), Department Of Agriculture
description: Code of Federal Regulations, Title 7 (Agriculture), Part 29 (Tobacco Inspection). Text from the eCFR as of 2026-10-26 (unofficial editorial compilation; the official edition is the annual CFR). Tobacco as it appears between the time it is cured and stripped from the stalk, or primed and cured, and the time it enters into the different manufacturing processes. The acts of stemming, threshing and sweating, and conditioning are not regarded as manufacturing processes.

title: 7 C.F.R. § 29.3070 — Tobacco products.
creator: Agricultural Marketing Service (Standards, Inspections, Marketing Practices), Department Of Agriculture
description: Code of Federal Regulations, Title 7 (Agriculture), Part 29 (Tobacco Inspection). Text from the eCFR as of 2026-10-26 (unofficial editorial compilation; the official edition is the annual CFR). Manufactured tobacco, including cigarettes, cigars, smoking tobacco, chewing tobacco, and snuff, which is subject to Internal Revenue tax.

title: 7 C.F.R. § 29.3071 — Type.
creator: Agricultural Marketing Service (Standards, Inspections, Marketing Practices), Department Of Agriculture
description: Code of Federal Regulations, Title 7 (Agriculture), Part 29 (Tobacco Inspection). Text from the eCFR as of 2026-10-26 (unofficial editorial compilation; the official edition is the annual CFR). A division of a class of tobacco having certain common characteristics and closely related grades. Tobacco which has the same characteristics and corresponding qualities, colors, and lengths is classified as one type, regardless of any factors of historical or geographical nature which cannot be.

title: 7 C.F.R. § 29.3072 — Undried.
creator: Agricultural Marketing Service (Standards, Inspections, Marketing Practices), Department Of Agriculture
description: Code of Federal Regulations, Title 7 (Agriculture), Part 29 (Tobacco Inspection). Text from the eCFR as of 2026-10-26 (unofficial editorial compilation; the official edition is the annual CFR). The condition of unfermented tobacco which has not been air-dried or steam-dried.

title: 7 C.F.R. § 29.3073 — Uniformity.
creator: Agricultural Marketing Service (Standards, Inspections, Marketing Practices), Department Of Agriculture
description: Code of Federal Regulations, Title 7 (Agriculture), Part 29 (Tobacco Inspection). Text from the eCFR as of 2026-10-26 (unofficial editorial compilation; the official edition is the annual CFR). An element of quality which describes the consistency of a lot of tobacco as it is prepared for market. Uniformity is expressed in grade specifications as a percentage. The percentage is applicable to group, quality, and color. (See Rule 13.).

title: 7 C.F.R. § 29.3075 — Unstemmed.
creator: Agricultural Marketing Service (Standards, Inspections, Marketing Practices), Department Of Agriculture
description: Code of Federal Regulations, Title 7 (Agriculture), Part 29 (Tobacco Inspection). Text from the eCFR as of 2026-10-26 (unofficial editorial compilation; the official edition is the annual CFR). A form of tobacco, including whole leaf and leaf scrap, from which the stems or midribs have not been removed.

title: 7 C.F.R. § 29.3076 — Variegated (K).
creator: Agricultural Marketing Service (Standards, Inspections, Marketing Practices), Department Of Agriculture
description: Code of Federal Regulations, Title 7 (Agriculture), Part 29 (Tobacco Inspection). Text from the eCFR as of 2026-10-26 (unofficial editorial compilation; the official edition is the annual CFR). Any leaf of which 20 percent or more of its surface is yellow, grayish, mottled, or bleached, and does not blend with the normal colors of the type or group and is generally characterized by a lower degree of leaf structure and maturity than.

title: 7 C.F.R. § 29.3077 — Wet (W).
creator: Agricultural Marketing Service (Standards, Inspections, Marketing Practices), Department Of Agriculture
description: Code of Federal Regulations, Title 7 (Agriculture), Part 29 (Tobacco Inspection). Text from the eCFR as of 2026-10-26 (unofficial editorial compilation; the official edition is the annual CFR). Any sound tobacco containing excessive moisture to the extent that it is in an unsafe or doubtful-keeping order. Wet applies to any tobacco which is not damaged but which is likely to damage if treated in the customary manner. (See Rule 22.).

title: 7 C.F.R. § 29.3078 — Width.
creator: Agricultural Marketing Service (Standards, Inspections, Marketing Practices), Department Of Agriculture
description: Code of Federal Regulations, Title 7 (Agriculture), Part 29 (Tobacco Inspection). Text from the eCFR as of 2026-10-26 (unofficial editorial compilation; the official edition is the annual CFR). The relative breadth of a tobacco leaf expressed in relation to its length. Width as an element of quality, does not apply to tobacco in strip form. (See Elements of quality.).

title: 7 C.F.R. § 29.3101 — Elements of quality and degrees of each element.
creator: Agricultural Marketing Service (Standards, Inspections, Marketing Practices), Department Of Agriculture
description: Code of Federal Regulations, Title 7 (Agriculture), Part 29 (Tobacco Inspection). Text from the eCFR as of 2026-10-26 (unofficial editorial compilation; the official edition is the annual CFR). These standardized words or terms are used to describe tobacco quality and to assist in interpreting grade specifications. Tobacco attributes or characteristics which constitute quality are designated as elements of quality. The range within each element is expressed by the use of words or.

title: 7 C.F.R. § 29.3103 — Rules.
creator: Agricultural Marketing Service (Standards, Inspections, Marketing Practices), Department Of Agriculture
description: Code of Federal Regulations, Title 7 (Agriculture), Part 29 (Tobacco Inspection). Text from the eCFR as of 2026-10-26 (unofficial editorial compilation; the official edition is the annual CFR). The application of these official standard grades shall be in accordance with the following rules.

title: 7 C.F.R. § 29.3104 — Rule 1.
creator: Agricultural Marketing Service (Standards, Inspections, Marketing Practices), Department Of Agriculture
description: Code of Federal Regulations, Title 7 (Agriculture), Part 29 (Tobacco Inspection). Text from the eCFR as of 2026-10-26 (unofficial editorial compilation; the official edition is the annual CFR). Each grade shall be treated as a subdivision of a particular type. When the grade is stated in an inspection certificate, the type also shall be stated.

title: 7 C.F.R. § 29.3105 — Rule 2.
creator: Agricultural Marketing Service (Standards, Inspections, Marketing Practices), Department Of Agriculture
description: Code of Federal Regulations, Title 7 (Agriculture), Part 29 (Tobacco Inspection). Text from the eCFR as of 2026-10-26 (unofficial editorial compilation; the official edition is the annual CFR). The determination of a grade shall be based upon a thorough examination of a lot of tobacco or of an official sample of the lot.

title: 7 C.F.R. § 29.3106 — Rule 3.
creator: Agricultural Marketing Service (Standards, Inspections, Marketing Practices), Department Of Agriculture
description: Code of Federal Regulations, Title 7 (Agriculture), Part 29 (Tobacco Inspection). Text from the eCFR as of 2026-10-26 (unofficial editorial compilation; the official edition is the annual CFR). In drawing an official sample from a hogshead or other package of tobacco, three or more breaks shall be made at such points and in such manner as the inspector or sampler may find necessary to determine the kinds of tobacco and the percentage.

title: 7 C.F.R. § 29.3107 — Rule 4.
creator: Agricultural Marketing Service (Standards, Inspections, Marketing Practices), Department Of Agriculture
description: Code of Federal Regulations, Title 7 (Agriculture), Part 29 (Tobacco Inspection). Text from the eCFR as of 2026-10-26 (unofficial editorial compilation; the official edition is the annual CFR). The grade assigned to any lot of tobacco shall be a true representation of the tobacco at the time of inspection and certification. If, at any time, it is found that a lot of tobacco does not comply with the specifications of the grade.

title: 7 C.F.R. § 29.3108 — Rule 5.
creator: Agricultural Marketing Service (Standards, Inspections, Marketing Practices), Department Of Agriculture
description: Code of Federal Regulations, Title 7 (Agriculture), Part 29 (Tobacco Inspection). Text from the eCFR as of 2026-10-26 (unofficial editorial compilation; the official edition is the annual CFR). A lot of tobacco on the marginal line between two colors shall be placed in the color with which it best corresponds with respect to body or other associated elements of quality.

title: 7 C.F.R. § 29.3109 — Rule 6.
creator: Agricultural Marketing Service (Standards, Inspections, Marketing Practices), Department Of Agriculture
description: Code of Federal Regulations, Title 7 (Agriculture), Part 29 (Tobacco Inspection). Text from the eCFR as of 2026-10-26 (unofficial editorial compilation; the official edition is the annual CFR). Any lot of tobacco which meets the specifications of two grades shall be placed in the higher grade. Any lot of tobacco on the marginal line between two grades shall be placed in the lower grade.

title: 7 C.F.R. § 29.3110 — Rule 7.
creator: Agricultural Marketing Service (Standards, Inspections, Marketing Practices), Department Of Agriculture
description: Code of Federal Regulations, Title 7 (Agriculture), Part 29 (Tobacco Inspection). Text from the eCFR as of 2026-10-26 (unofficial editorial compilation; the official edition is the annual CFR). A lot of tobacco meets the specifications of a grade when it is not lower in any degree of any element of quality than the minimum specifications of such grade.

title: 7 C.F.R. § 29.3111 — Rule 8.
creator: Agricultural Marketing Service (Standards, Inspections, Marketing Practices), Department Of Agriculture
description: Code of Federal Regulations, Title 7 (Agriculture), Part 29 (Tobacco Inspection). Text from the eCFR as of 2026-10-26 (unofficial editorial compilation; the official edition is the annual CFR). In determining the grade of a lot of tobacco, the lot as a whole shall be considered. Minor irregularities which do not affect over one percent of the tobacco shall be overlooked.

title: 7 C.F.R. § 29.3112 — Rule 9.
creator: Agricultural Marketing Service (Standards, Inspections, Marketing Practices), Department Of Agriculture
description: Code of Federal Regulations, Title 7 (Agriculture), Part 29 (Tobacco Inspection). Text from the eCFR as of 2026-10-26 (unofficial editorial compilation; the official edition is the annual CFR). Any special factor symbol, approved by the Director of the Tobacco Division of the Agricultural Marketing Service, may be used to show a peculiar side or characteristic of the tobacco which tends to modify the grade.

title: 7 C.F.R. § 29.3113 — Rule 10.
creator: Agricultural Marketing Service (Standards, Inspections, Marketing Practices), Department Of Agriculture
description: Code of Federal Regulations, Title 7 (Agriculture), Part 29 (Tobacco Inspection). Text from the eCFR as of 2026-10-26 (unofficial editorial compilation; the official edition is the annual CFR). Interpretations, the use of specifications, and the meaning of terms shall be in accordance with determinations or clarifications made by the Chief of the Standards Branch and approved by the Director.

title: 7 C.F.R. § 29.3114 — Rule 11.
creator: Agricultural Marketing Service (Standards, Inspections, Marketing Practices), Department Of Agriculture
description: Code of Federal Regulations, Title 7 (Agriculture), Part 29 (Tobacco Inspection). Text from the eCFR as of 2026-10-26 (unofficial editorial compilation; the official edition is the annual CFR). The use of any grade may be restricted by the Director during any marketing season, when it is found that the grade is not needed or appears in insufficient volume to justify its use.

title: 7 C.F.R. § 29.3115 — Rule 12.
creator: Agricultural Marketing Service (Standards, Inspections, Marketing Practices), Department Of Agriculture
description: Code of Federal Regulations, Title 7 (Agriculture), Part 29 (Tobacco Inspection). Text from the eCFR as of 2026-10-26 (unofficial editorial compilation; the official edition is the annual CFR). Any lot, except strip form, of Leaf (B Group) tobacco in which 20 percent or more of its leaves are under 16 inches in length shall be designated as Tips (T Group).

title: 7 C.F.R. § 29.3116 — Rule 13.
creator: Agricultural Marketing Service (Standards, Inspections, Marketing Practices), Department Of Agriculture

The percentages shall govern the portion of a lot which must meet the specifications of the grade. The minor portion must be closely related but may be of a different group, quality, and color.

creator: Agricultural Marketing Service (Standards, Inspections, Marketing Practices), Department Of Agriculture

Tobacco damaged under 20 percent but which otherwise meets the specifications of a grade shall be treated as a subgrade by placing the special factor “U” after the grademark. This special factor does not apply to tobacco designated as “No-G.”.

creator: Agricultural Marketing Service (Standards, Inspections, Marketing Practices), Department Of Agriculture
description: Code of Federal Regulations, Title 7 (Agriculture), Part 29 (Tobacco Inspection). Tobacco shall be designated as No Grade, using the grademark, “No-G,” when it is dirty, offtype, semicured, needs to be reworked, damaged 20 percent or more, contains foreign matter, or has an odor foreign to the type.

creator: Agricultural Marketing Service (Standards, Inspections, Marketing Practices), Department Of Agriculture
description: Code of Federal Regulations, Title 7 (Agriculture), Part 29 (Tobacco Inspection). Text from the eCFR as of 2026-10-26 (unofficial editorial compilation; the official edition is the annual CFR). Tobacco in Type 31 shall be designated by the grademark “No-G-Nested” when it is nested.

creator: Agricultural Marketing Service (Standards, Inspections, Marketing Practices), Department Of Agriculture

description: Code of Federal Regulations, Title 7 (Agriculture), Part 29 (Tobacco Inspection). creator: Agricultural Marketing Service (Standards, Inspections, Marketing Practices), Department Of Agriculture
description: Code of Federal Regulations, Title 7 (Agriculture), Part 29 (Tobacco Inspection). Cured leaves from this stalk position have a tendency to roll, concealing the stem or midrib. Lugs or Cutters have an oblate to rounded tip and are usually thin to medium.

description: Code of Federal Regulations, Title 7 (Agriculture), Part 29 (Tobacco Inspection). Extremely common tobacco which does not meet the minimum specifications or which exceeds the tolerance of the lowest grade of any other group.

creator: Agricultural Marketing Service (Standards, Inspections, Marketing Practices), Department Of Agriculture
description: Code of Federal Regulations, Title 7 (Agriculture), Part 29 (Tobacco Inspection). Scrap accumulates from handling tobacco in farm buildings, warehouses, packing and conditioning plants, and stemmeries.

Text from the eCFR as of 2026-10-26 (unofficial editorial compilation; the official edition is the annual CFR). As used in §§ 29.3501 to 29.3686, the words and phrases hereinafter defined shall have the indicated meanings so assigned.

creator: Agricultural Marketing Service (Standards, Inspections, Marketing Practices), Department Of Agriculture
description: Code of Federal Regulations, Title 7 (Agriculture), Part 29 (Tobacco Inspection). Text from the eCFR as of 2026-10-26 (unofficial editorial compilation; the official edition is the annual CFR). Tobacco cured under natural atmospheric conditions without the use of fire, except for the purpose of preventing pole-burn in damp weather.

description: Code of Federal Regulations, Title 7 (Agriculture), Part 29 (Tobacco Inspection). description: Code of Federal Regulations, Title 7 (Agriculture), Part 29 (Tobacco Inspection). (See Elements of Quality, § 29.3586.).

creator: Agricultural Marketing Service (Standards, Inspections, Marketing Practices), Department Of Agriculture
description: Code of Federal Regulations, Title 7 (Agriculture), Part 29 (Tobacco Inspection). Text from the eCFR as of 2026-10-26 (unofficial editorial compilation; the official edition is the annual CFR). A group of colors ranging from a light brown to a dark brown. These colors vary from medium to low saturation and from medium to very low brillance. As used in these standards, the colors are expressed as light brown (L), medium brown (F).

creator: Agricultural Marketing Service (Standards, Inspections, Marketing Practices), Department Of Agriculture
description: Code of Federal Regulations, Title 7 (Agriculture), Part 29 (Tobacco Inspection). Text from the eCFR as of 2026-10-26 (unofficial editorial compilation; the official edition is the annual CFR). A major division of tobacco based on method of cure or principal usage.

title: 7 C.F.R. § 29.3507 — Clean.
creator: Agricultural Marketing Service (Standards, Inspections, Marketing Practices), Department Of Agriculture
description: Code of Federal Regulations, Title 7 (Agriculture), Part 29 (Tobacco Inspection). Text from the eCFR as of 2026-10-26 (unofficial editorial compilation; the official edition is the annual CFR). Tobacco is described as clean when it contains only a normal amount of sand or soil particles. Leaves grown on the lower portion of the stalk normally contain more dirt or sand than those from higher stalk positions. (See Rule 4, § 29.3605.).

title: 7 C.F.R. § 29.3508 — Color.
creator: Agricultural Marketing Service (Standards, Inspections, Marketing Practices), Department Of Agriculture
description: Code of Federal Regulations, Title 7 (Agriculture), Part 29 (Tobacco Inspection). Text from the eCFR as of 2026-10-26 (unofficial editorial compilation; the official edition is the annual CFR).
